issue_creates.title: Worker lifecycle: preserve ownership, cancellation and cleanup across replay
issue_creates.body:
## Problem and required outcome

Replay workers must remain owned through startup, running/paused work, failures/recovery, cancellation and exit. The checked audit found concrete lifecycle defects, including recovery after cancellation, lost live-child ownership after interrupted waits, dead-owner IPC locks and incorrect reaping. Deliver the lifecycle children under this epic while preserving healthy process isolation and cleanup.

This epic stays open until every required child and shared gate is complete. Filing issues or publishing a PR is not delivery. The stale-event child is an explicitly qualified investigation: completion requires a deterministic confirmation plus correction, or a documented disproof and regression invariant.

## Evidence and confidence

[Full checked audit](https://github.com/robinwassen/Fossilize/blob/c039c2b6c9997e78a6a4dd46df5ff1534eda7a62/local-docs/reviews/worker-lifecycle-audit.md) · [Runnable probes, retained outputs and independent checker reports](https://github.com/robinwassen/Fossilize/blob/c039c2b6c9997e78a6a4dd46df5ff1534eda7a62/local-docs/reviews/worker-lifecycle-audit-evidence/README.md).

The audit used a rules-research agent, separate Linux-controller and external-owner inspectors, independent cross-checkers and primary-agent reruns. Thirteen expected Linux observations matched, including negative controls. Actual API/production-function probes are distinguished from extracted-helper mechanisms, modeled races and source-only conditional branches. Windows findings have independent source/OS review but no native execution. No finding is attributed to a particular historical Steam report or installed client version.

Audited upstream source: `556da9ff7d7616704dda515756219ab1dab693ec`. The relevant platform lifecycle headers remain unchanged in fork master `5eb2c496dde819c868fa3d7d1e52c51047d9adb8`; evidence snapshot: `c039c2b6c9997e78a6a4dd46df5ff1534eda7a62`.

## Shared acceptance gates

- Each child states its exact violated lifecycle boundary, affected platform, evidence strength, reproduction or proposed injection, required outcome and scope. Maintain those qualifications during implementation.
- Register deterministic assertion-bearing tests with the project's runner/CI. Prefer barriers, controllable workers, explicit syscall/API fault injection and fake clocks over sleeps or random driver instability. Include success controls and before-fix failure where feasible.
- Assert actual process liveness, ownership, exit collection, descriptor/handle lifetime, cancellation admission and bounded completion as relevant. Logs alone are not an oracle. Test crash/cancellation ordering, stopped workers and partial startup.
- Declare source, binary, protocol and behavioral compatibility at every affected public boundary. Preserve documented once-only start and reaping/group-use preconditions unless explicitly changing and testing them. No silent result/layout change or invented old guarantee.
- Run applicable Debug/Release and exception-enabled/disabled configurations. Linux and Windows implementations require their own platform-specific evidence. Unavailable native Windows/device checks remain unavailable/incomplete rather than passing. GPU-independent subprocess/mocks are the baseline; no GPU or Steam change is required merely to prove an ownership defect.
- Keep normal parent-death cleanup, healthy cancellation/reaping, normal recovery, intentionally inherited protocol descriptors and successful work reuse functioning. Do not treat fixed partitions, deliberately paused processes or zombies as evidence of active orphan workers.

## Relationship to existing work

Do not duplicate observability's result-schema obligations. Existing https://github.com/robinwassen/Fossilize/issues/13 covers retained child loss, https://github.com/robinwassen/Fossilize/issues/22 and https://github.com/robinwassen/Fossilize/issues/23 cover authoritative completion/results, and https://github.com/robinwassen/Fossilize/issues/24 covers cancellation reporting. This epic owns the process/IPC control defects; coordinate shared behavior through those issues without reparenting them.

## Ordering and scope

Prioritize cancellation/restart prevention and external wait/reap ownership, then dead-owner IPC and launcher lifetime, then startup transactions/descriptor inheritance and phase supervision. This is sequencing advice, not invented blocking dependencies between otherwise independent fixes. Native parent/sub-issues provide grouping; no child is ready or complete solely because it belongs here.

Scope includes replay external owner/API, progress wrapper, Linux/Windows supervisor and worker startup/recovery/teardown. Excludes a broad scheduler/work-stealing rewrite, memory budgets, Steam-side scheduling/presentation, deployment, and capture-layer recorder work. Apple/Android robust modes are not supported by the current build; do not manufacture coverage claims.

## Running the retained Linux evidence

On Linux with GCC, Python 3 and populated project submodules, check out evidence commit `c039c2b6c9997e78a6a4dd46df5ff1534eda7a62` from this fork and run:

```sh
git submodule update --init --recursive
python3 local-docs/reviews/worker-lifecycle-audit-evidence/reproduce.py --out /tmp/fresh-fossilize-lifecycle-evidence
```

The output directory must not already exist. Inspect the named case in `results.json`; generated binaries also accept the case arguments shown there. No Steam or real GPU workload is started. The runner matches observed defects, so a successful research-run exit does not certify corrected behavior.

issue_creates.title: Prevent worker recovery from restarting work after cancellation
issue_creates.body:
## Problem

A worker can exit with recoverable code 2 immediately before cancellation. shutdown_processes sets expect_kill and sends SIGKILL, but that cannot change the already-exited child status. process_shutdown suppresses retry only for a SIGKILL status, so it requests recovery; the reaper starts another process after cancellation.

## Evidence level

Reproduced using actual production shutdown/recovery functions with a real exited child and controlled recovery markers. Two independent checkers validated the replacement call chain. This is not a full Steam/event-loop reproduction.

## Reproduction / verification status

Run the shared runner; inspect `cancel-actual`, `cancel_control`, and `cancel_live_control`. The first uses WNOWAIT to establish exit 2 before cancellation, then calls actual shutdown_processes and process_shutdown. Observed `expect_kill=1 replacement_requested=1`. Cancelling a live worker is the successful negative control: `restart_requested=0`.

[Probe source](https://github.com/robinwassen/Fossilize/blob/c039c2b6c9997e78a6a4dd46df5ff1534eda7a62/local-docs/reviews/worker-lifecycle-audit-evidence/cancel_actual.cpp)

## Running the retained Linux evidence

On Linux with GCC, Python 3 and populated project submodules, check out evidence commit `c039c2b6c9997e78a6a4dd46df5ff1534eda7a62` from this fork and run:

```sh
git submodule update --init --recursive
python3 local-docs/reviews/worker-lifecycle-audit-evidence/reproduce.py --out /tmp/fresh-fossilize-lifecycle-evidence
```

The output directory must not already exist. Inspect the named case in `results.json`; generated binaries also accept the case arguments shown there. No Steam or real GPU workload is started. The runner matches observed defects, so a successful research-run exit does not certify corrected behavior.

## Required outcome and acceptance

- Once cancellation is observed, no worker start or recovery admission may occur, regardless of the pending exit status or delayed IPC.
- Cover cancellation through SIGINT/SIGTERM and control EOF, crash-before-cancel, cancel-before-crash, stopped workers, and normal completion. Use barriers, not a race lottery.
- Retain/reap every existing owned child and expose cancellation separately from successful replay. Coordinate reporting with https://github.com/robinwassen/Fossilize/issues/24 rather than duplicating its result-schema work.

## Scope and references

Fix/investigate the lifecycle boundary described above, including its regression coverage. Do not expand this into Steam scheduling policy, automatic deployment, a general scheduler rewrite or unrelated Vulkan behavior.

issue_creates.title: Keep ownership of a live replayer when wait is interrupted
issue_creates.body:
## Problem

A handled signal without SA_RESTART interrupts the child-tree sentinel read in ExternalReplayer::wait(). The implementation logs the error, polls waitpid for about 100 ms, synthesizes success 0, and resets its PID while the child is still running.

## Evidence level

Reproduced against the unmodified ExternalReplayer implementation; independently rebuilt and rerun.

## Reproduction / verification status

Run the shared runner and inspect `external wait-interrupt`. A controlled helper stays alive; SIGALRM interrupts wait. Observed `wait_status=0 child_alive=1 handle=-1`. The harness individually kills/reaps its child afterwards.

[Probe source](https://github.com/robinwassen/Fossilize/blob/c039c2b6c9997e78a6a4dd46df5ff1534eda7a62/local-docs/reviews/worker-lifecycle-audit-evidence/external_probe.cpp)

## Running the retained Linux evidence

On Linux with GCC, Python 3 and populated project submodules, check out evidence commit `c039c2b6c9997e78a6a4dd46df5ff1534eda7a62` from this fork and run:

```sh
git submodule update --init --recursive
python3 local-docs/reviews/worker-lifecycle-audit-evidence/reproduce.py --out /tmp/fresh-fossilize-lifecycle-evidence
```

The output directory must not already exist. Inspect the named case in `results.json`; generated binaries also accept the case arguments shown there. No Steam or real GPU workload is started. The runner matches observed defects, so a successful research-run exit does not certify corrected behavior.

## Required outcome and acceptance

- Retry EINTR or return a truthful interruption outcome without forgetting the live child; never synthesize successful completion from a live waitpid result.
- Use a deterministic signal/barrier test and assert process liveness, retained ownership, eventual cancellation/reaping and final status.
- Cover already-dead children, normal EOF, repeated wait after completion and fatal/nonretryable errors. Preserve the documented wait contract or explicitly document/test an intentional change.

## Scope and references

Fix/investigate the lifecycle boundary described above, including its regression coverage. Do not expand this into Steam scheduling policy, automatic deployment, a general scheduler rewrite or unrelated Vulkan behavior.

issue_creates.title: Recover lifecycle handling when a shared IPC lock owner dies
issue_creates.body:
## Problem

The diagnostic FIFO uses a nonrobust shared futex with no owner-death recovery. A controller killed while holding the lock leaves it acquired. poll_progress can reap that dead controller and then block acquiring the same lock; wait pumps progress before completion handling and can also block.

## Evidence level

Reproduced using the actual ExternalReplayer API/shared block and production futex. A controlled helper forces the owner-death state; an independent checker reran it. No frequency in real Steam/driver crashes is established.

## Reproduction / verification status

Run the shared runner and inspect `owner-lock`. Its helper maps the real shared block, sets progress_started, acquires the production lock, and exits 37. The caller observes exit with WNOWAIT then polls. Observed `poll_returned=0 subject_alive=1 wait_channel=futex...`. A scoped supervisor kills only its own blocked test process.

[Probe source](https://github.com/robinwassen/Fossilize/blob/c039c2b6c9997e78a6a4dd46df5ff1534eda7a62/local-docs/reviews/worker-lifecycle-audit-evidence/owner_lock.cpp)

## Running the retained Linux evidence

On Linux with GCC, Python 3 and populated project submodules, check out evidence commit `c039c2b6c9997e78a6a4dd46df5ff1534eda7a62` from this fork and run:

```sh
git submodule update --init --recursive
python3 local-docs/reviews/worker-lifecycle-audit-evidence/reproduce.py --out /tmp/fresh-fossilize-lifecycle-evidence
```

The output directory must not already exist. Inspect the named case in `results.json`; generated binaries also accept the case arguments shown there. No Steam or real GPU workload is started. The runner matches observed defects, so a successful research-run exit does not certify corrected behavior.

## Required outcome and acceptance

- Controller death while holding the IPC lock must not indefinitely block progress, cancellation or completion queries.
- Choose explicit owner-death/corrupt-ring handling; do not blindly clear a possibly live lock or report damaged IPC as trustworthy success.
- Test dead controller and dead polling thread with host still alive, ordinary contention, damaged/incomplete messages, and normal progress. Keep diagnostic failure independent of lifecycle ownership.

## Scope and references

Fix/investigate the lifecycle boundary described above, including its regression coverage. Do not expand this into Steam scheduling policy, automatic deployment, a general scheduler rewrite or unrelated Vulkan behavior.

issue_creates.title: Align replayer parent-death protection with owning process lifetime
issue_creates.body:
## Problem

PR_SET_PDEATHSIG follows the Linux thread that called fork, not the entire parent process. Starting ExternalReplayer from a temporary std::thread and allowing that thread to exit kills replay even while the owning object and application remain alive. The public API specifies no launching-thread lifetime restriction.

## Evidence level

Reproduced through the unmodified API; checked against Linux parent-death semantics. This causes premature termination, not surviving workers.

## Reproduction / verification status

Run the shared runner and inspect `external thread`. Keep ExternalReplayer in main, call start from a temporary thread, wait until the helper starts, return/join that thread. Observed `host_alive=1 child_signaled=1 signal=9`.

[Probe source](https://github.com/robinwassen/Fossilize/blob/c039c2b6c9997e78a6a4dd46df5ff1534eda7a62/local-docs/reviews/worker-lifecycle-audit-evidence/external_probe.cpp)

## Running the retained Linux evidence

On Linux with GCC, Python 3 and populated project submodules, check out evidence commit `c039c2b6c9997e78a6a4dd46df5ff1534eda7a62` from this fork and run:

```sh
git submodule update --init --recursive
python3 local-docs/reviews/worker-lifecycle-audit-evidence/reproduce.py --out /tmp/fresh-fossilize-lifecycle-evidence
```

The output directory must not already exist. Inspect the named case in `results.json`; generated binaries also accept the case arguments shown there. No Steam or real GPU workload is started. The runner matches observed defects, so a successful research-run exit does not certify corrected behavior.

## Required outcome and acceptance

- A supported temporary launcher thread must not accidentally determine the child lifetime; establish and document the actual owner boundary.
- Preserve cleanup after whole-owner-process death and cover death before/after protection registration.
- Test launching-thread exit while owner remains alive, whole-process normal/crash/forced death, and ordinary cancellation. Declare compatibility impact if introducing a thread-affinity restriction.

## Scope and references

Fix/investigate the lifecycle boundary described above, including its regression coverage. Do not expand this into Steam scheduling policy, automatic deployment, a general scheduler rewrite or unrelated Vulkan behavior.

issue_creates.title: Collect replay exit status once without reaping unrelated host children
issue_creates.body:
## Problem

is_process_complete reaps replay then calls poll_progress, which attempts a second wait and overwrites the exit status with -ECHILD. wait also calls poll_progress first; if that reaps replay/reset_pid, its later waitpid uses -1 and can collect an unrelated host child.

## Evidence level

Both paths reproduced against the unmodified API and independently rerun. Applies to a child exiting before progress_complete, such as early failure; normal published completion follows a different path.

## Reproduction / verification status

Run the shared runner. `external status`: helper exit 37 becomes `done=1 status=-10 expected=37`. `external wait-steals-child`: both replay exit 37 and unrelated exit 42 are synchronized with WNOWAIT; wait returns 42, and a later host waitpid on its unrelated child returns ECHILD.

[Probe source](https://github.com/robinwassen/Fossilize/blob/c039c2b6c9997e78a6a4dd46df5ff1534eda7a62/local-docs/reviews/worker-lifecycle-audit-evidence/external_probe.cpp)

## Running the retained Linux evidence

On Linux with GCC, Python 3 and populated project submodules, check out evidence commit `c039c2b6c9997e78a6a4dd46df5ff1534eda7a62` from this fork and run:

```sh
git submodule update --init --recursive
python3 local-docs/reviews/worker-lifecycle-audit-evidence/reproduce.py --out /tmp/fresh-fossilize-lifecycle-evidence
```

The output directory must not already exist. Inspect the named case in `results.json`; generated binaries also accept the case arguments shown there. No Steam or real GPU workload is started. The runner matches observed defects, so a successful research-run exit does not certify corrected behavior.

## Required outcome and acceptance

- Centralize collection so one owned child is reaped once and cached terminal status is stable across poll/is_process_complete/wait.
- Never use waitpid(-1) as an accidental consequence of reset ownership; unrelated host child status must remain available to its owner.
- Test early exit, ordinary complete marker, repeated terminal queries and legitimate external SIGCHLD/reaper interference; report unknown status honestly instead of fabricating success.

## Scope and references

Fix/investigate the lifecycle boundary described above, including its regression coverage. Do not expand this into Steam scheduling policy, automatic deployment, a general scheduler rewrite or unrelated Vulkan behavior.

issue_creates.title: Roll back resources acquired during failed external replayer startup
issue_creates.body:
## Problem

ExternalReplayer startup has local pipe/socket descriptors that are not closed if a later acquisition or fork fails. Failure of the second pipe leaks the first pipe endpoints even after object destruction. Earlier named shared-memory creation also needs failure-path cleanup.

## Evidence level

Second-pipe failure reproduced by controlled linker syscall injection. Other socket/fork and early shm-name paths are source-proven omissions, not individually executed cases.

## Reproduction / verification status

Run the shared runner and inspect `external pipe-failure`. A linker wrapper injects EMFILE on the second pipe call. start returns false; destroy the object; descriptor count remains two above baseline: `start=0 ... leaked=2`.

[Probe source](https://github.com/robinwassen/Fossilize/blob/c039c2b6c9997e78a6a4dd46df5ff1534eda7a62/local-docs/reviews/worker-lifecycle-audit-evidence/external_probe.cpp)

## Running the retained Linux evidence

On Linux with GCC, Python 3 and populated project submodules, check out evidence commit `c039c2b6c9997e78a6a4dd46df5ff1534eda7a62` from this fork and run:

```sh
git submodule update --init --recursive
python3 local-docs/reviews/worker-lifecycle-audit-evidence/reproduce.py --out /tmp/fresh-fossilize-lifecycle-evidence
```

The output directory must not already exist. Inspect the named case in `results.json`; generated binaries also accept the case arguments shown there. No Steam or real GPU workload is started. The runner matches observed defects, so a successful research-run exit does not certify corrected behavior.

## Required outcome and acceptance

- Every partial startup failure releases owned descriptors, mappings, names and handles; any already-started child must retain an explicit cleanup/reap path.
- Inject failure at each acquisition boundary and assert stable resource counts after destruction; include shm namespace cleanup and fork failure.
- Preserve the documented once-only start contract; repeated-start misuse is not this issue. Controller-process-local leaks should be distinguished from host-lifetime leaks.

## Scope and references

Fix/investigate the lifecycle boundary described above, including its regression coverage. Do not expand this into Steam scheduling policy, automatic deployment, a general scheduler rewrite or unrelated Vulkan behavior.

issue_creates.title: Restrict inherited descriptors so one replay cannot retain another owner sentinel
issue_creates.body:
## Problem

A second ExternalReplayer instance inherits the first instance host-side control sender across exec. Closing the intended owner sender then does not produce EOF until the unrelated second process releases its copy, delaying controller ownership-loss detection.

## Evidence level

Reproduced with two supported API instances and controlled helpers. This establishes descriptor/sentinel interference; the destructor does not explicitly promise to terminate the child, so no such guarantee is assumed.

## Reproduction / verification status

Run the shared runner and inspect `external inherited-control`. Helper A waits for EOF on its passed control fd. Start helper B, destroy owner A, then terminate/reap B. Observed `after_A_destroyed_A_alive=1 after_B_killed_A_exited=1`.

[Probe source](https://github.com/robinwassen/Fossilize/blob/c039c2b6c9997e78a6a4dd46df5ff1534eda7a62/local-docs/reviews/worker-lifecycle-audit-evidence/external_probe.cpp)

issue_creates.title: Keep fault-module bootstrap transfer from blocking controller cancellation
issue_creates.body:
## Problem

The Linux controller synchronously writes accumulated failing-module hashes before closing its own redundant input-pipe reader and before entering supervision. A dead/stalled replacement plus enough hashes fills the pipe; the controller-held reader prevents EPIPE. Blocked SIGTERM and control EOF cannot be serviced while that write is stuck.

## Evidence level

Unchanged production-helper mechanism reproduced; independent checker added a successful negative control closing the redundant reader. Requires a sufficiently large accumulated blacklist and a replacement that stops consuming it. Not a whole-replayer or Steam reproduction.

## Reproduction / verification status

Run the shared runner and inspect `blacklist_pipe` and `blacklist_control`. A real child exits before reading 4096 synthetic module hashes. Observed `returned_before_SIGTERM=0 returned_after_SIGTERM=0 controller_exited=0`; closing the redundant reader removes this mechanism. External SIGKILL still terminates the controller.

[Probe source](https://github.com/robinwassen/Fossilize/blob/c039c2b6c9997e78a6a4dd46df5ff1534eda7a62/local-docs/reviews/worker-lifecycle-audit-evidence/blacklist_pipe.cpp)

## Running the retained Linux evidence

On Linux with GCC, Python 3 and populated project submodules, check out evidence commit `c039c2b6c9997e78a6a4dd46df5ff1534eda7a62` from this fork and run:

```sh
git submodule update --init --recursive
python3 local-docs/reviews/worker-lifecycle-audit-evidence/reproduce.py --out /tmp/fresh-fossilize-lifecycle-evidence
```

The output directory must not already exist. Inspect the named case in `results.json`; generated binaries also accept the case arguments shown there. No Steam or real GPU workload is started. The runner matches observed defects, so a successful research-run exit does not certify corrected behavior.

## Required outcome and acceptance

- Close unused pipe ends before transfer and ensure startup IPC cannot indefinitely block supervisor event handling.
- Use bounded/nonblocking bootstrap transfer or equivalent lifecycle-aware startup with explicit errors/deadlines.
- Test a full pipe, dead/stalled reader, partial/EINTR writes, cancellation/control EOF during bootstrap, and successful replacement. Cover Windows equivalent bootstrap behavior where applicable.

## Scope and references

Fix/investigate the lifecycle boundary described above, including its regression coverage. Do not expand this into Steam scheduling policy, automatic deployment, a general scheduler rewrite or unrelated Vulkan behavior.

issue_creates.title: Investigate stale epoll events being applied to replacement worker slots
issue_creates.body:
## Problem

epoll data identifies a reusable slot without a generation. Reaping can restart that slot while an already-returned event batch still contains old pipe/timer events. Dispatch then resolves the new descriptor and can perform a blocking read on it.

## Evidence level

Treat this as an investigation with a required proof/disproof outcome, not an established frequency or Steam cause. An independent checker confirmed epoll documents this event-cache pitfall.

Observed `stale_event_dispatch_returned=0`. This deliberately imposes the schedule and does not prove it occurred in the full event loop.

issue_creates.title: Add Windows supervision deadlines outside pipeline batch compilation
issue_creates.body:
## Problem

Windows workers emit BEGIN_HEARTBEAT and HEARTBEAT but the controller parser recognizes neither and has no heartbeat watchdog. Its only timer starts after CRASH. The batch no-completion timeout therefore does not bound hung initialization, other preparation, or final driver destruction.

## Evidence level

Two independent source/OS reviews agree on the coverage gap. No native Windows binary or real driver hang was executed. A universal deadline is a required reliability improvement, not an existing documented guarantee.

## Reproduction / verification status

Inspect the Windows parser/ProcessProgress and infinite wait set, then compare emitted heartbeat messages. Proposed native reproduction: controllable worker hangs before CRASH during init or final teardown; assert controller can detect and terminate within a configured policy. This native experiment remains unexecuted.

## Required outcome and acceptance

- Define bounded supervision for startup, active execution and final teardown without mistaking deliberate pauses or legitimate long work for failure.
- Handle heartbeat messages or implement an equivalent supervised liveness protocol; keep compilation no-progress timeout distinct.
- Add deterministic native Windows subprocess tests for startup/teardown hangs, normal long compilation, crash cleanup and cancellation. Unavailable native evidence leaves acceptance incomplete.

## Scope and references

issue_creates.title: Handle abandoned Windows IPC mutex ownership without retaining the lock
issue_creates.body:
## Problem

IPC code enters/releases the named mutex only for WAIT_OBJECT_0. WAIT_ABANDONED also grants ownership, so the survivor skips ReleaseMutex and can retain the mutex indefinitely, blocking other participants after a thread dies while holding it.

## Evidence level

Two independent source reviews checked Microsoft semantics: WAIT_ABANDONED grants ownership and recursive acquisitions need matching releases. Requires owner-thread death inside the critical section. No native Windows reproduction.

## Reproduction / verification status

Proposed native test: a controlled thread/process acquires the IPC mutex and terminates; a survivor receives WAIT_ABANDONED, then another participant tries to poll. Inspect the WAIT_OBJECT_0-only branches. The native failure injection was not executed in this audit.

## Required outcome and acceptance

- Handle abandoned ownership explicitly, validate/reject potentially inconsistent FIFO state, and release ownership or make a controlled terminal transition.
- Do not merely treat abandonment as ordinary successful data without validating consistency.
- Test owner-thread death with host still alive, controller death, repeated same-thread polling and a different subsequent polling thread; assert no lifecycle wait is stranded. Require native Windows evidence.

## Scope and references

Fix/investigate the lifecycle boundary described above, including its regression coverage. Do not expand this into Steam scheduling policy, automatic deployment, a general scheduler rewrite or unrelated Vulkan behavior.

issue_creates.title: Give Windows worker IPC failures an explicit lifecycle transition
issue_creates.body:
## Problem

The Windows controller discards false from process_once. ResetEvent/GetOverlappedResult/rearming failures can leave a living worker without usable communication or supervision; without a preexisting crash timer, the controller may wait indefinitely. A failed reset may instead leave a signaled event spinning.

## Evidence level

Source-proven conditional handling gap, independently reviewed. No triggering Windows API failure was executed. A worker that exits normally still has its process handle to signal completion; no claim that every pipe error leaks a worker.

## Reproduction / verification status

Proposed native fault injection: keep a worker alive, fail ResetEvent, GetOverlappedResult or the next overlapped read, then request cancellation/observe controller state. Assert a bounded explicit terminal/recovery transition. Not run during this audit.

## Required outcome and acceptance

- Distinguish expected pipe EOF associated with exit from loss of communication with a still-live worker.
- On unrecoverable IPC failure, preserve ownership and enter bounded cancellation/recovery; do not silently wait forever or spin.
- Add native Windows subprocess tests for each injected I/O failure, normal EOF, concurrent exit, crash timer and cancellation. Coordinate heartbeat/deadline behavior with the sibling supervision issue without assuming parent membership is a blocking dependency.

## Scope and references

Fix/investigate the lifecycle boundary described above, including its regression coverage. Do not expand this into Steam scheduling policy, automatic deployment, a general scheduler rewrite or unrelated Vulkan behavior.
